skill.name: landing-experience-checker
skill.description: Checks a paid ad destination page before launch. It compares ad promises with page content, above-the-fold visibility, speed evidence, form friction, and mobile rendering.
skill.summary: Preflight landing pages for ad message match, speed, form friction, and mobile readiness.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline labels, metadata URLs, and fixed repository links. One finding is confirmed: the rendered-page read example uses a shell command with a user-supplied URL, which needs validation and safe argument handling before publication.

remediation.issue: Shell command template accepts a user-provided landing URL.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the shell string with a connector API call or argument-array execution. Validate that the URL is http or https, quote arguments, and reject shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: Rendered-page crawling can fetch arbitrary campaign URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation that the destination is owned or authorized before using the crawler, especially with the own-site option.

remediation.issue: The saved report path uses a page placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Specify that the page value must be normalized to a safe filename and kept inside memory/ad/landing-experience-checker/.

remediation.issue: Repository-relative Markdown links trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearer repository-root references or state that these links are documentation references, not runtime file traversal.

content.value_statement: Ad campaigns can launch with weak message match, slow pages, or mobile issues. This skill checks the destination page against ad promises and returns a practical pass/fix report.
actual_capabilities: Compares ad headlines and hooks with the landing page offer and value proposition.
Checks whether the promised offer and primary CTA appear above the fold.
Reads supplied PageSpeed or CrUX data, or labels speed and mobile checks as estimated.
Counts required form fields and identifies specific friction points.
Marks each check as Pass, Partial, or Fix with a named repair owner.
Creates a handoff summary for follow-up landing page work.
limitations: It does not rewrite page copy, redesign forms, or restructure the page.
It does not compute an account score or make the final launch decision.
It needs a destination URL or pasted page copy and the related ad copy.
Speed and mobile results are estimated unless measured data is supplied.

use_cases.title: Pre-Launch Campaign Check
use_cases.description: Review a destination page before paid ads go live and catch message-match gaps early.

use_cases.title: Landing Experience Diagnosis
use_cases.description: Identify whether offer mismatch, slow load, form friction, or mobile rendering may hurt Quality Score.

use_cases.title: Page Repair Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a concise punch list that tells copy, design, or offer owners what needs repair.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Preflight
prompt_templates.prompt: Preflight this landing page before launch: [URL]. Compare it with these ad headlines: [headlines]. Mark each check Pass, Partial, or Fix.

prompt_templates.title: Message Match Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [URL] against these ad promises: [offer, price, product, audience]. Flag every promise the page does not clearly honor.

prompt_templates.title: Quality Score Diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: This campaign has below-average landing-page experience. Review [URL] and this ad copy: [copy]. Identify the likely failing lever and the owner.

prompt_templates.title: Measured Launch Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pasted PageSpeed or CrUX metrics, mobile render notes, and ad copy below to audit [URL]. Label each metric as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated.

output_examples.input: A launch URL and three search ad headlines for a new paid campaign.
output_examples.output: The report marks message match as Partial, above-the-fold as Pass, speed as Estimated, form friction as Fix, and mobile as Pass. It routes the form issue to the page owner.

output_examples.input: A campaign with below-average landing-page experience and no speed export.
output_examples.output: The report asks for measured speed data, labels speed and mobile as Estimated, and still checks the offer, CTA, and form friction.

output_examples.input: An ad promising a discount while the page promotes a consultation.
output_examples.output: The report flags an offer mismatch, blocks launch readiness, and routes the canonical offer question to the offer registry owner.

best_practices: Provide the final ad headlines and the destination page together.
Include PageSpeed, CrUX, or mobile render evidence when available.
Require every Fix to name the exact gap and the repair owner.
anti_patterns: Treating estimated speed or mobile checks as measured results.
Asking the skill to rewrite page copy or redesign the form.
Launching after a generic Fix that lacks a specific gap and owner.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks message match, above-the-fold offer visibility, speed evidence, form friction, and mobile rendering.

faq.question: Does it redesign the landing page?
faq.answer: No. It identifies gaps and routes repair work to the right owner or sibling skill.

faq.question: Does it need paid tools?
faq.answer: No. It can use pasted page copy, user-provided exports, or keyless page reads when available.

faq.question: Can it use PageSpeed data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use PageSpeed or CrUX data and label each metric as measured, user-provided, or estimated.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide a destination URL or pasted page copy, plus the ad headlines or hooks that point to the page.

faq.question: How are results delivered?
faq.answer: Results are delivered as a Pass, Partial, or Fix punch list with a short handoff summary.
